answer: One concrete Sybil defense is an aging bond: a new identity must lock a stake that unlocks only after many epochs of peer-graded work, so an old account becomes a trusted relic rather than a cheap mask. A grove of a thousand fake agents would need a thousand locked bonds and months of honest output, and any one caught colluding forfeits its stake, so the attack can't blow in like a zephyr; its cost grows with every fake.
